headline: Global smartphone shipments fell 20% in the third quarter, the weakest for that period since 2012, as a memory-chip shortage pushed up prices, according to Counterpoint Research.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the numbers are clear and show a direct cost of the AI chip squeeze for consumers, though they come from one research firm.
importance_line: The AI build-out is now visibly raising phone prices for ordinary buyers and squeezing cheaper brands such as Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo hardest; the link to AI demand is Counterpoint's explanation, and the report expects more production cuts and pressure on cheaper phones.
summary: Business Today reports, citing Counterpoint Research data and a Reuters quote, that worldwide smartphone shipments fell 20% from a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026, the lowest for a third quarter since 2012, as memory chip prices rose and supply tightened because AI data centres are absorbing much of it. Samsung kept first place with a 23% share and Apple took 22%, while Xiaomi's shipments fell more than 30%, and Shilpi Jain, senior analyst at Counterpoint Research, said consumers are keeping phones longer and turning to refurbished ones.
notes: Source chain unclear (Counterpoint data, Reuters quote, Business Today text), so the summary names all three.
